label: L-03
title: Sub-unit backlog is unreachable once emissions stop: 0 < owed < scale with non-zero principal reverts 'nothing to annihilate', and no other reward path is open
description: netWanted == 0 and excess == 0, so the require at :545 reverts. With antimatterPerDay at 0 the backlog can never grow past `scale`, and with claimEnabled false claim() is shut, so the user has NO reward path: claim shut, autoAnnihilate reverts, and emergencyWithdraw zeroes the backlog at :702 (N4).
impact: Liveness failure for a bounded amount. Bounded by `scale`, hence Low.
severityBasis: C4 Low: reward-path liveness, value bounded by one `scale` unit.
recommendation: Allow a sub-unit backlog to be swept, or fold it forward rather than reverting.

relatedNotDuplicate.title: A zero-principal backlog holder has NO reward path at all on a Migrating pool while claimEnabled is false
relatedNotDuplicate.ruling: KEPT SEPARATE per the classifier. SAME FAMILY ('no reward path exists in state X'), DIFFERENT PRECONDITIONS: fb7a089a is ZERO principal on a MIGRATING pool; L-03 is NON-ZERO principal, sub-unit owed, on an ACTIVE pool with emissions stopped. Different trigger, different fix. A human at /ledger may choose to merge; an agent may not.

relatedNotDuplicate.relation: REBIRTH ON A NEW REVERT SITE
relatedNotDuplicate.why: L-03 is the rebirth of 7e86c0cf's dust-window liveness class. The old revert ('exit shortfall' on a sub-share-price amount) was deleted with previewExitFor; the class survives on a DIFFERENT revert site: 0 < owed < scale now trips require(netWanted > 0 || excess > 0) -> 'nothing to annihilate'. Same family, new mechanism, new fingerprint -- recorded explicitly so the rebirth does not hide inside a moot disposition.
